title: Correlation of immunological processes and electrophysiological activity in temporal lobe epilepsy of non-neoplastic origin
summary:
Epilepsy is one of the most common serious chronic neurological diseases, affecting 0.7% of the population in all age groups and stages of life.
Inflammatory processes in brain tissue have been increasingly associated with the development of epilepsy in recent years. So far, it is not possible to make a statement before an operation as to whether the tissue that could potentially trigger epilepsy is showing inflammatory changes. If a connection between abnormalities in brain wave measurements and inflammatory brain tissue changes could be demonstrated, this might be possible.
We would therefore first like to compare the various options for brain wave recording deep in the brain (these are regularly used before a possible surgical procedure in order to be able to more precisely define the area that triggers epilepsy before an operation) and test their use during an open operation.
We are looking for a connection between markers from brain wave recording and inflammatory tissue changes. To do this, we would first like to examine tissue from previous operations and compare it with the stored brain wave measurements. We would also like to collect tissue directly before future deep brainwave recordings and correlate it with the respective recording; here, no tissue changes that would influence the results would be expected due to the implantation of these deep electrodes or a subsequent operation.
We would like to correlate all results with the clinical parameters, i.e. with the type and duration of the epilepsy, the outcome after surgery, among other things.
conditions: temporal lobe epilepsy of non-neoplastic origin

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Archive cohort
- All patients who have been evaluated presurgically using sEEG since the founding of the Rhein-Main Epilepsy Center in 2015 and subsequently undergone epilepsy surgery.
Prospective cohort:
- All patients who are scheduled for sEEG/microwire implantation
- All patients who are scheduled for epilepsy surgery in the temporal lobe area with an indication for intraoperative electrophysiological determination of the resection margin.
Exclusion criteria:
- Suspected malignant neoplasm in the temporal lobe
- Inflammatory disease of the central nervous system (CNS)
- History of meningitis / encephalitis less than 12 months ago
